planting.note: Start indoors early alongside a favorite scion variety; graft the two together once stems are pencil-thick, heal in a humid shaded chamber, then transplant after frost into full sun.

directions: This exceptionally vigorous interspecific hybrid rootstock is grown to be grafted onto a favorite heirloom or hybrid tomato scion, not eaten itself, offering a much larger and more disease-resistant root system that in turn boosts scion vigor, fruit size, total yield, and season length compared to an ungrafted plant on its own roots. Widely used in commercial greenhouse and high tunnel tomato production, it carries broad resistance to soil-borne diseases including fusarium wilt, verticillium wilt, and corky root rot, extending productive plant life well past what many own-root tomatoes achieve in intensive production. Start rootstock and scion seed together indoors, graft when stems are pencil-thick using a tube or splice graft, keep grafted plants in a humid, shaded healing chamber for about a week, then harden off and transplant after frost into full sun with sturdy staking or trellising to support the extra vigor.

directions: This vigorous interspecific hybrid rootstock is grown to be grafted onto a favorite tomato scion variety rather than eaten itself, valued for a somewhat more moderate, better-balanced vigor than the extremely aggressive Maxifort rootstock, making it a popular choice where growers want the disease resistance and yield benefits of grafting without excessive vegetative growth crowding out fruit production. It carries strong resistance to fusarium and verticillium wilts, corky root rot, and nematodes, and its more restrained root vigor compared to Maxifort suits closer plant spacing or shorter growing seasons where overly rampant rootstock growth would be a liability. Start rootstock and scion seed together indoors, graft when stems are pencil-thick, heal grafted plants in a humid, shaded chamber for about a week, then harden off and transplant after frost into full sun with sturdy support.

common_name: Torvum Vigor Rootstock Eggplant (Turkey Berry Rootstock)

planting.note: Start indoors well ahead of the scion variety, since seed germinates slowly and unevenly, then graft a favorite eggplant scion onto it once stems are pencil-thick, heal in a humid shaded chamber, and transplant after frost into full sun.

directions: This wild, thorny relative of eggplant is grown as a grafting rootstock rather than for its own small, bitter fruit, valued for an exceptionally vigorous, deep root system that confers strong resistance to bacterial wilt, fusarium wilt, verticillium wilt, and root-knot nematodes, all serious soil-borne problems that shorten the productive life of own-root eggplant in warm, humid climates. Grafting a favorite eggplant scion onto this rootstock is a traditional practice in parts of Asia and is gaining adoption among home and market growers in the humid Gulf South seeking longer-lived, more disease-resistant eggplant plants without resorting to soil fumigation or long rotations. Start rootstock seed well ahead of the scion, since germination is slower and less even than standard eggplant, graft when stems are pencil-thick, heal grafted plants in a humid, shaded chamber for about a week, then harden off and transplant after frost into full sun with sturdy support.

planting.note: Start indoors alongside a favorite watermelon, melon, or cucumber scion, timing sowing so both are the same stem thickness at grafting; graft, heal in a humid shaded chamber, then transplant after frost into full sun.

directions: This vigorous interspecific hybrid squash rootstock is grown to be grafted onto a favorite watermelon, melon, or cucumber scion rather than eaten itself, providing a much larger, more aggressive root system that confers strong resistance to fusarium wilt and other soil-borne diseases along with improved tolerance of cool soil, drought, and salinity compared to a plant grown on its own roots. Widely used in commercial watermelon production in Asia and increasingly adopted by market and home growers elsewhere, grafted watermelon plants on this rootstock often show extended harvest windows, larger overall plant size, and better performance in soils with a history of vine crop disease. Start rootstock and scion seed together indoors, timing sowing so stem diameters match at grafting time, graft using a hole-insertion or splice technique, heal grafted plants in a humid, shaded chamber for about a week, then harden off and transplant after frost into full sun on raised beds or hills.
